title: One Corridor, 108 Windows, No Two Alike — Suzhou Garden | China Travel Expert
description:
One garden corridor holds 108 lattice windows — and no two share the same design.

Canglang Pavilion (the Surging Wave Pavilion) is the oldest of Suzhou's classical gardens, dating to the Northern Song dynasty almost a thousand years ago. Its Double Corridor runs over 100 meters, and each of its 108 latticed windows is cut in a different shape — square, fan, peach, vase, leaf — so the same garden looks new through every frame. The Classical Gardens of Suzhou joined the UNESCO World Heritage list in 2000.

🧭 Expert Tip: Arrive right at opening — Suzhou's gardens are near-empty in the first hour and packed by midday.
